correctness.rationale: Subdivide each edge once: essential vertices are separated by at least two edges and the shortest cycles have eight edges, sufficient for the three-particle cubical model. The inclusion is natural for the 72 whole-graph automorphisms. A new cubical enumeration of unordered cells with disjoint closures gives (455,1404,1386,432), all boundary squares zero, and ranks (454,946,432) modulo 97. Over Q the first rank is at most 454 by augmentation, the last at most 432 by dimension. Particle-sum sends the four loops moving one particle around fundamental rectangles, with two particles fixed on the complementary edges, to a basis of graph H1. This forces the middle rank to be at most 1404−454−4=946. Hence the modular lower bounds are all exact over Q. The particle-sum map identifies H1 with the tensor of the two augmentation subspaces of the permutation representations on the parts, with minus flip from reversal of graph edges. Signed fixed-cube traces were independently verified for all 72 elements, with the product of edge orientation signs and the permutation sign of the edge factors. They give 1−χ1+χ2 for the stated formulas. On the part-preserving subgroup the extra H2 terms are the two exchanged inducing characters; they vanish off that subgroup. Rational semisimplicity and character equality give the stated modules; averaging yields no positive-degree invariant classes. The quotient conclusion follows from rational averaging on an invariant triangulation: the fat diagonal is a subcomplex in a simultaneous subdivision of the ordered graph product, and its complement has an equivariant simplicial model after barycentric subdivision, also allowing particle permutations.
residual_risks: The reduced Świątkowski computation was not replayed separately; the cubical check gives a separate proof of the relevant ranks and character. No integral H2 torsion conclusion is drawn.
